messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: Upper Critical Temperature
parts:
Hey Mike,

I was hoping you could clarify some terminology. I've been trying to locate the right numbers to input for TC_MAX on some species, and I've been running into upper critical temperature (UCT). Some sources are saying it's the maximum body temperature that can be tolerated by an organism, which would suggest that it is the parameter I'm looking for. However, other sources are specifying that it's just the upper bound of the thermo-neutral zone, which would suggest that it isn't TC_MAX (particularly since in some cases the reported UCT is lower then the normal body temperature of the animal in question!).

Is this not the right number to use for TC_MAX?

Thank you!
Adam

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Upper Critical Temperature
parts:
Hi Adam,

For endotherms, upper critical temperature refers to the air temperature, not the body temperature. See attached for a discussion about why upper critical temperature really isn't a functional trait. TC_MAX is how high you allow your animal to let its core temperature go as part of physiological thermoregulation. Does that answer your question?

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Upper Critical Temperature
parts:
Hi Adam - in the endotherm model, TC_MAX is the maximum it allows the body temperature to go as part of its thermoregulatory response. By implication, if all other options are exhausted and the predicted metabolic rate remains below basal, then the animal would have overheated past the the TC_MAX and died.
All the best,
Mike
